items_missed: 1_set_agenda: Never explicitly checked/confirmed the move date works for the customer, and no 'sound good?' confirmation after the opening agenda statement.

2_probe: Didn't ask about additional rooms/storage, special considerations (narrow hallways, tight turns), storage stops, extra stops, access/parking concerns, or moving stressors; addresses were recapped but zip codes were never confirmed.
3_pricing: No 'pricing is super simple' opener, no Meet Your Mover mention, no On-Time Guarantee mention.
4_clock: Never explained that the clock starts on-site when the contract opens.
5_estimate: Didn't tie stairs/floors into the time variability, no walk-distance mention, no size equivalents used (e.g., school bus reference).

6_save_your_ass: No concrete consolidation examples (toys, garden tools, drawer items, wall photos) and no 'take a carload' tip — only a general 'stage boxes near the door' comment, which doesn't count as the full prep speech.
7_quote_booking: Didn't attempt to lock in the date on the call, no mention of a bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email, and didn't ask the customer to reply with corrections.
9_bonus: No genuine rapport/laugh moment, and didn't pair the No Worries damage coverage explanation with the 60¢/lb baseline liability comparison.
top_strength: Amy's pricing walkthrough was thorough and specific — she gave the exact hourly rate, the one-time travel fee, and a clear low-to-high price range ($1,305–$1,513) tied to hours, then repeated "no additional fees of any type" more than once, which is exactly the reassurance a customer on a long-distance quote needs to trust the number.
coaching_note: You're strong on pricing clarity and proactive FAQs, but you're leaving real points on the table in three places: give the full Save Your Ass speech with an actual example (consolidating drawer items, taking a carload yourself) instead of just "stage boxes near the door"; work Meet Your Mover and the On-Time Guarantee into every pricing section — they're free trust-builders and you skipped both; and don't let "I'll decide by Monday" close the call without at least asking if he wants to lock the date in today, since there's no deposit required.
phone_presence_notes: Consistent warm affirmations ("Sure, no worries," "Sounds good," "Take your time") and a friendly close kept the customer comfortable and responsive throughout, though there was no standout humor or rapport moment to push it to a 5.
